statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the block threshold while Stress stays high on conflicting cross-asset signals and a scheduled post-close memory-sector report.
recommendation: Tail is in the watch band and below the block threshold. The narrow flagged window covers the 20:00Z cash close through 22:00Z, spanning quarter-end marks and a scheduled memory-sector fiscal Q4 report in thinning liquidity.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a two-way advance after soft August PCE, with quarter-end marks and a post-close memory report as the near-term checkpoints
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,549.67, up 0.69%, inside a 30,415.16-30,630.45 range after opening at 30,421.68. NQ futures at 30,832.50 (+0.72%) first traded below their 30,657.25 open to 30,512.25, then recovered to within roughly 73 points of the 30,905.50 high. That completed retracement, together with VIX at 15.83 near its session low, indicates mean reversion is still functioning rather than a persistent one-way path, which keeps Tail in the watch band. August PCE printed softer than expected at 3.4% year over year against 3.7% anticipated, with core PCE at 3.0% versus 3.3%, and the repricing has been orderly. Fed commentary describing no urgency on an October move has cut implied October hike odds to roughly 41% from above 70% a week earlier. Stress remains high because cross-asset signals conflict with the equity advance: the 10-year yield rose about five basis points to 5.30% despite the softer inflation data, Brent trades near $98.28 and WTI near $90.58 on continued uncertainty around U.S.-Iran negotiations, and leadership is narrow with the Dow lower while the Nasdaq gains. The main unresolved forward item is a scheduled memory-sector fiscal Q4 report after the 20:00Z cash close, arriving alongside quarter-end marks; guidance was framed at about $50 billion of revenue and an 86% gross margin, and the sector carries meaningful index weight. That constitutes a credible delayed second-information-wave mechanism into thin liquidity, so it is reflected in Stress and a narrow flagged window rather than in a pre-print Tail escalation. Federal funding was extended through December 11, removing an October 1 lapse as a near-term amplifier. Shared Finviz context was stale at collection and marked partial, so it was excluded and the assessment rests on directly verified sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail eased from 20 to 15 across the overnight and European hours as volatility decayed, then rebuilt from 15 to a 23 peak through the U.S. morning as the PCE release and quarter-end approached, easing to 22 in the prior hour. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 65 and 73. Mode was mixed for most of the window with a short normal stretch late on September 29.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to hold in the watch band through the 20:00Z cash close and the post-close memory-sector report, peaking at 24 between 20:00Z and 22:00Z without crossing the block threshold, because no post-print price path is observed yet and event importance alone is treated as a Stress input. Tail is then projected to decay into the low band across the Asian and European sessions as event flow empties, before rebuilding to 20 for the 12:30Z jobless-claims slot and to a 23 second-day peak at the 14:00Z ISM manufacturing release, which lands half an hour into the U.S. cash session. The final hour eases ahead of scheduled non-farm payrolls the following morning. Confidence drifts from 87 to 80 with forecast distance.
